editorialAssessment.storyForm: PASS: concrete actions, relationships, cause, loneliness, fear, humor and pressure carry the story; no reader coaching, invented dialogue or mechanical chapter-label list.
editorialAssessment.depths: Essential and Core coherently stop at the announced final exam. Core adds supported scenes; Deep supplies withheld consequences and original-novel coda. Screen count is not treated as a quota.
editorialAssessment.ethicalMeaning: Ender’s deterrent violence, distress and incomplete knowledge remain distinct from deliberate adult manipulation and adult justification. No categorical moral absolution, Kessel verdict or asserted definitive authorial intent.
editorialAssessment.sourceAdequacy: PASS for the particular retained story at declared limits; no essential unsupported hinge identified. Guide-backed links are not mislabeled complete primary reading. Absence of continuous full-edition reading is not used as a blanket rejection.
editorialAssessment.bilingualParity: REQUIRES-FIXES: EG-EN-001. Names, actions, relationships and outcome boundaries otherwise materially agree.
editorialAssessment.scienceHistoryClinical: Fictional ansible/weapon/alien model is not offered as real science. No clinical diagnosis, historical analogy or imported certainty.

findings.category: translation clarity / ambiguous object in a supported physical event
findings.exactRUClause: Эндер хватает его руку; в невесомости мальчика уносит к стене, рука ломается.
findings.exactENClause: Ender grabs his arm; in null gravity the boy flies into a wall and breaks it.
findings.reason: The immediate English antecedent of “it” is “a wall”, so the sentence readily says Bernard breaks the wall. The supported event and unambiguous RU say his arm breaks. This is a small required referent correction, not evidence of an invented shuttle scene.

minimumSupportedCorrection.en: Ender grabs his arm; in null gravity the boy flies into a wall and breaks his arm.
